note: City of Burnaby 2026 PROPERTY TAX NOTICE, folio 5395-6128-0065. The FIRST property tax notice in the corpus, added with the `propertytax` sub_bill_type (commercial-narrative-v11). Until this document the corpus held no tax notice at all, so nothing could detect a regression on the family that accounted for 21 of the 26 misrouted payables in the 2026-08-27 B2 audit. || sub_bill_type 'propertytax' is the point of this anchor: measured on a scratch analyzer across all six sample tax notices (Abbotsford, Burnaby, Richmond, Surrey, Vancouver x2), both twins agreed at 0.858-0.892 on every one, while the controls held (burnaby_water->water, business_license->business_license, bchydro->electric). Before v11 both prompts routed property tax to 'other' by an explicit rule. || Values verified against the page: vendor 'City of Burnaby' from the letterhead; service_address '14E 6128 PATTERSON AVE' is the taxed parcel; total 2,428.69 is the largest printed figure and the balance owing (the page also prints 1,276.29 / 1,583.69 / 1,858.69, which are levy subtotals and grant-adjusted variants); payment_due_date from 'DUE DATE: Friday, July 3, 2026'; invoice_date from 'Mailing Date: May 29, 2026' (both twins, 0.782 / 0.683). account_number is the printed FOLIO / ROLL. || invoice_number 'property_burnaby' is the municipal filename fallback -- the notice prints no invoice number -- so it tracks this file's NAME; rename the PDF and this assertion must change with it. || Verifiable absences: gst_amount is null on both twins (a tax notice charges no GST, so amount_excluding_gst is absent too), no billing period is printed, and the five narrative fields are '' by design on the municipal bucket. || NOT asserted: invoice_description, measured UNSTABLE across 3 replicates ('2026 property tax notice.' twice, 'Annual property tax charges for 2026.' once). || NOT asserted either: the raw invoice_date twins. They were asserted briefly and measured UNSTABLE on the first live pass -- invoice_date_extract returned null on 1 of 3 reads. The RESOLVED writeValues.invoice_date is stable across all three (the generate twin is corroborated against the printed 'Mailing Date: May 29, 2026'), and that is the value that reaches Dynamics, so it is asserted and the noisy twins beneath it are not. Note 'Mailing Date' is NOT one of find_invoice_date_in_text's accepted labels, so the printed-label fallback cannot rescue this document if BOTH twins ever fail together. || routingDecision is NOT asserted (dropped 2026-08-28, user-approved). This document is the ONLY one of the six property tax notices that prints a row labelled 'Amount due' carrying three DIFFERENT figures -- $2,428.69 / $1,858.69 / $1,583.69 for no grant / regular grant / senior grant. 'Amount due' is the strongest cue for total_invoice_amount, and the analyzer prompt has no rule for home-owner-grant columns (defect A11), so the EXTRACT twin -- which must emit a span pointing at one figure -- either anchors weakly (0.415-0.609, the lowest of all six notices) or declines outright, returning the A9 empty shape on 3 of 6 cached reads. No other notice ever loses it (0/6 each): surrey prints an 'Amount due' row too but all three columns are the SAME number, and the other four print no such row at all, anchoring instead on TOTAL TAXES PAYABLE / TOTAL TAXES DUE. Losing the extract twin removes the AGREEMENT boost, which is what actually carries every one of these six -- none reliably clears the 0.73 bar alone (property_richmond passes at extract 0.415 / generate 0.341 purely by agreement). The lone generate twin must then clear 0.73 by itself and swings 0.316-0.746, so 1 read in 6 fails B4 and routes to review. The VALUE is correct on every read and total_invoice_amount 2428.69 IS still asserted, along with the other 18 writeValues -- only the decision is not. Asserting HAPPY_PATH_CANDIDATE would assert that a document printing three candidate figures under its own 'Amount due' label always auto-writes to Dynamics with no human involved, which is not a property worth guaranteeing; B4 sending it to review is the gate working. Restore this assertion if A11 ships and the extract twin anchors reliably. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice. || account_number is written WITHOUT the 'Account No: ' prefix on this family (user requirement, 2026-09-09, propertytax ONLY -- every other municipal bill and every commercial invoice keeps the label). The written value is the bare folio, which is what an owner quotes to the municipality.
